rationale: Both share the same coprimality check and grouping approach. A is a bit more idiomatic. It computes the modular inverse with Python's built-in pow(a, -1, M) instead of B's hand-written brute-force search, which also duplicates the coprime error. A's flat isalpha/isdigit branches are clearer than B's nested isalnum-then-isdigit checks. A lowercases each letter in both encode and decode. B's decode does not lowercase its input, so uppercase ciphertext would decode incorrectly. A's main wart is in its grouping expression. It re-joins the whole character list on every 5-character slice, and it reuses the name i, which hurts both clarity and efficiency. B joins once before slicing. On balance A's built-in inverse, simpler branching and consistent case handling outweigh that blemish.
